Local word autocomplete and next-word prediction for the **OpenCode V2** prompt composer — inspired by [oh-my-pi (OMP)](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi)'s n-gram text prediction engine. As you type, Quill predicts the remainder of your current prose word or the next word in sequence, shown as dimmed inline ghost text directly at your cursor. Press Tab or → to accept it, or Esc to dismiss.

**Install:** add `"opencode-quill"` to `plugins` in `~/.config/opencode/cli.json` and restart OpenCode ([details](#install)). ## What it does - **Zero AI, completely local:** Runs entirely on-device without sending prompt text to any model, API, or external service. - **Context-aware ranking:** Blends a common-English vocabulary prior with an online n-gram model (bigrams and trigrams) learned from your prompt history. - **Completes words, fixes typos, and predicts next words:** Completes the active prose prefix, offers single-edit corrections, and predicts following words when learned evidence supports the sequence. - **Ghost-text styling:** Matches [opencode-ghost](https://github.com/ozandogrultan/opencode-ghost)'s dimmed appearance (the theme's muted text color), rendered in the OpenTUI buffer without displacing the cursor. - **Safe acceptance:** Inserts or corrects the active word in the draft without submitting. Supports native undo (Ctrl+- or Cmd+Z). Never overwrites unrelated draft text and never touches the system clipboard. - **Coexists with Ghost:** [Ghost](https://github.com/ozandogrultan/opencode-ghost) suggests entire next prompts in an *empty* composer using a model; Quill predicts words in an *active* draft locally. When both are installed, each activates only in its respective domain without key conflicts. - **Prose-aware gating:** Automatically suppresses suggestions in code blocks, backticks, file paths, URLs, slash commands, active selections, and modal dialogs. Hyphenated words (`read-only`), brand names (`OpenCode`, `GitHub`) and bare filenames with common extensions (`install.sh`) count as prose; identifiers (`showSidebar`), flags and `key=value` tokens do not. - **Shell mode:** In the prompt's shell mode Quill completes commands, subcommands and flags from a separate vocabulary learned from the commands you ran, never from prose. Shell completion is case-sensitive, never corrects typos, and skips paths, quoted strings, `$` expansions, assignments and any command that mentions a token, secret, password, passphrase, key, cookie or credential, passes a password flag (`curl -u user:pass`, `mysql -p…`, `sshpass -p`, `docker login -p`), or contains a recognisable API token (`sk-`, `ghp_`, `glpat-`, `xoxb-`, JWT, AWS key ID). Attachment and pasted-text chips are treated as non-prose: words are still suggested after them, but never inside them, and typo replacements are not offered while a chip is present. - **End-of-draft by default:** Suggestions appear on a partial word or after a space at the end of the draft. Opt-in logical-line-end completion can also append a suffix or next word immediately before a newline, preserving later lines. It never suggests in the middle of a line or at a visual wrap boundary. ## What suggestions look like The suggestion appears dimmed at the cursor, at the end of the draft or an opt-in logical line end. It is not part of the editable text until you press Tab or →. | Kind | Your draft | Dimmed suggestion | Draft after acceptance | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Word completion | `please comp` | `lete` | `please complete` | | Typo correction | `please cmplete` | ` → complete` | `please complete` | | Next word | `please run ` | `tests` | `please run tests` | A correction looks like this, with only ` → complete` dimmed: ```text > please cmplete → complete ``` - **Completions append** the missing letters or next word. - **Corrections replace only the active word**, preserving its initial-capital or all-uppercase casing (`Cmplete` → `Complete`, `CMPLETE` → `COMPLETE`). First-person contractions use a capital `I` in corrections and next-word suggestions (`I'm`, `I'll`, `I've`, `I'd`). Lowercase contraction prefixes are replaced on acceptance too (`i'v` → `I've`). - **Learned casing is kept.** A word you usually capitalize mid-sentence is suggested that way: `oz` shows ` → Ozan` and replaces the word, while `Oz` completes with `an`. - **Normal completions take precedence.** For example, `whate` completes to `whatever` rather than being corrected to `what`. Typo correction is a fallback when no confident prefix completion is available; recognized words are not corrected. - **Earlier words are never rewritten.** With learned evidence for `please run tests`, typing `please rnu ` can suggest `tests`. Accepting it produces `please rnu tests`, leaving `rnu` unchanged. ## Quill or Ghost? | | quill | [ghost](https://github.com/ozandogrultan/opencode-ghost) | | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | | Suggests | the rest of the current word, or the next word | your whole next prompt | | When | while you type a draft | the composer is empty, after a turn | | How | a local n-gram model, no network | a small model reads the recent conversation | | Model calls | none | one per turn | Install both: each activates only in its own domain, with no key conflicts. ## Requirements - [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) with the V2 TUI plugin runtime (the supported range is `engines.opencode` in `package.json`). - Node.js (for the installer script). ## Install ### From npm (recommended) Add the package to `plugins` in `~/.config/opencode/cli.json`: ```jsonc { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/v2/cli.json", "plugins": [ "opencode-quill" ] } ``` OpenCode installs the package and its dependencies on the next start. ### From this repository ```sh git clone https://github.com/ozandogrultan/opencode-quill.git cd opencode-quill bun install ./install.sh ``` Restart OpenCode to load it. `install.sh` copies the plugin and its local vocabulary into `/plugins/opencode-quill/` and registers that directory in `/cli.json`. Unrelated plugins and configuration are preserved. To target a specific configuration directory: ```sh ./install.sh /path/to/config/opencode ``` ### Manually Add the plugin directory to `plugins` in `~/.config/opencode/cli.json`: ```jsonc { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/v2/cli.json", "plugins": [ "/absolute/path/to/opencode-quill/src" ] } ``` To pass custom options: ```jsonc { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/v2/cli.json", "plugins": [ { "package": "/absolute/path/to/opencode-quill/src", "options": { "enabled": true, "completeAtLineEnd": true, "acceptKeys": ["tab", "right"], "dismissKeys": ["escape"] } } ] } ``` Restart OpenCode after editing `cli.json`. ## Options | Option | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | Initial default for suggestions and learning; a persisted `/quill` toggle takes precedence. | | `completeAtLineEnd` | `boolean` | `false` | Also append completions or next words immediately before a newline within a draft. | | `completeShell` | `boolean` | `true` | Initial default for shell-mode suggestions and learning; a persisted `/quill shell` toggle takes precedence. | | `minSuggestedWordLength` | `number` | `0` | Minimum number of characters in a suggested word, for both prose and shell suggestions; `0` allows any length. | | `acceptKeys` | `string[]` | `["tab", "right"]` | Keys that accept and insert the active word suggestion. | | `dismissKeys` | `string[]` | `["escape"]` | Keys that dismiss the visible suggestion without inserting. | | `cycleNextKeys` | `string[]` | `[]` | Optional keys for the next confident word suggestion. | | `cyclePreviousKeys` | `string[]` | `[]` | Optional keys for the previous confident word suggestion. | `completeAtLineEnd` uses prose context only up to the cursor while checking code and attachment ranges across the full draft. It inserts only missing letters or a next word, without replacing typed text. Typo and casing replacements remain limited to chip-free draft ends. The suggestion must fit the visible cursor row; it never overwrites the next line. Acceptance preserves later lines, attachment metadata, host callbacks, and native undo/redo. Cycling changes only the ghost text; Tab still accepts the selected suggestion. Alternatives use the same confidence and typo guards as the best suggestion. The ranked list is capped at five, wraps in either direction, and resets when the draft, cursor, attachment ranges, or learned model changes. Alternatives that do not fit the visible cursor row are skipped. Without a visible, eligible alternative, cycle keys fall through to OpenCode. Custom keybindings can also be overridden using OpenCode's standard `keybinds` map in `cli.json`: ```jsonc { "keybinds": { "quill.accept": "ctrl+y", "quill.dismiss": "ctrl+g", "quill.next": "alt+n", "quill.previous": "alt+p" } } ``` Quill's accept/dismiss/cycle layer runs in base mode at priority `2`, only in the focused normal composer. A visible suggestion takes Tab/Right for acceptance and Escape for dismissal. With no eligible visible suggestion, commands return `false` or are disabled so host dispatch continues. Host autocomplete that captures navigation suppresses Quill; its Tab and Escape handlers remain in control. Dialogs and selections also suppress Quill. ## Commands - `/quill` — Toggle word autocomplete on or off (persisted across sessions). - `/quill on` / `/quill off` — Set autocomplete explicitly. - `/quill shell on` / `/quill shell off` — Set shell-mode autocomplete explicitly. - `/quill clear casing` (alias `/quill reset casing`) — Forget only the learned word casing (`OpenCode`, `GitHub`), keeping the vocabulary and phrases. - `/quill clear` (alias `/quill reset`) — Erase everything Quill has learned from your prompts and shell commands. - `quill.next` / `quill.previous` — Keymap commands for cycling visible word alternatives; no default bindings. Configure the cycle options above or OpenCode's `keybinds` map. - **Command Palette (`Ctrl+P`)** — Includes **Word autocomplete: on/off** and **Clear word autocomplete history**. ## How it works ### Learning Quill learns from your own submitted prompts, never from assistant output: - It listens to session events (`session.execution.started`, `session.execution.succeeded`, `session.inbox.delivered`). - On startup and when you open a session, it also backfills from the user messages of the current and most recently updated sessions. - Each message is ingested once, tracked by `:`. All processed IDs, including those of ignored pastes, are retained until `/quill clear`. - Only prose is learned. Code blocks, inline code, URLs, file paths, identifiers, slash commands, shell lines, indented blocks that do not continue a list item, and very large pastes are ignored. - Commands you run in shell mode are learned into a separate shell model from the session's shell messages, on the same triggers and with the same deduplication. Only plain words and flags are kept. - Punctuation, line breaks and code reset the context, so words separated by syntax are never learned as adjacent. - A word missing from the base vocabulary becomes suggestible only after it has been seen more than once, and not while it is a prefix of a learned word you use at least as often (`addr` yields to `addressed`). - Casing is learned from words written mid-sentence; sentence-initial capitals are ignored. ### Prediction - **Baseline prior:** a bundled English word-frequency table (SUBTLEX) gives useful completions from the first keystroke. - **Personal model:** unigram, bigram and trigram counts from your prompts. Context evidence falls back from trigram to bigram to unigram as it thins out. - **Current draft:** words already in the draft get a small boost. - **Confidence gating:** a suggestion is shown only when it clears a confidence threshold, which is stricter for next-word predictions than for prefix completions. If the typed prefix is already the most likely word, nothing is shown. - **Typo fallback:** when prefix completion is not confident enough, nearby words are ranked with an edit penalty and a stricter confidence threshold. Correction confidence is the edit-penalized model score. Suggestions must clear an absolute evidence floor and a separate candidate-dominance check. Corrections require at least three typed letters. Short words are eligible only for whole-word letter swaps that preserve the first letter; other edits and mistyped longer prefixes require at least five letters, except for apostrophe contractions, including missing apostrophes. Deletions repair only doubled letters, not arbitrary extra characters or word endings. Unknown tokens such as `json`, `yaml`, `bool`, `opts`, and `enum` are left unchanged, and uncertain typos such as `fucn` can produce no suggestion. Context repair uses the same edit guards and confidence checks and requires repeated learned continuation evidence; not every typo produces a suggestion. - **Bounded counts:** the personal model is pruned to its most frequent entries when saved. Once it holds about 100,000 learned words, every count is halved and single-use entries are dropped, so recent habits outweigh old ones. ### Storage Quill uses OpenCode's durable plugin storage, which writes JSON under the XDG state directory (`$XDG_STATE_HOME` when set, otherwise `~/.local/state`): | Data | File | | --- | --- | | Learned model | `opencode//tui/plugin.quill.learning.json` | | Learned shell model | `opencode//tui/plugin.quill.shell.json` | | Settings | `opencode//tui/plugin.quill.settings.json` | The learned models hold word, bigram, trigram and word-casing counts plus processed message IDs. These include local one-to-three-word fragments from your prose, so the model can reveal parts of your prompts. Quill does not store raw prompts or full message bodies. These files stay on your machine and are never tracked in Git or published to npm. `/quill clear` erases both learned models; the persisted on/off settings are separate. The processed-ID ledger is not pruned: its memory usage, stored size, and full serialization cost grow with the number of processed messages. Word and context counts remain bounded. Existing version-1 snapshots keep their counts and retained IDs without a reset. IDs absent from older capped snapshots cannot be recovered, so those messages may be learned again when backfilled. ## Development ```sh bun install bun run test # Unit tests and changelog checks bun run typecheck # Type verification (tsc --noEmit) bun run lint:sh # Syntax verification on shell scripts ``` ## More OpenCode plugins - [sesh](https://github.com/ozandogrultan/opencode-sesh) — search, preview, and resume every session across every project. - [ghost](https://github.com/ozandogrultan/opencode-ghost) — suggests your next prompt as ghost text in the empty composer. - [ember](https://github.com/ozandogrultan/opencode-ember) — prices a cold prompt-cache rewrite before you send. ## Contributing Contributions are welcome. Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) before submitting a pull request. ## License [MIT](LICENSE) © Ozan Dogrultan

# Changelog

All notable changes are documented in this file using
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/) and
[Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/).

## [0.7.0] - 2026-11-14

### Added

- **options:** Add minSuggestedWordLength (#22)

## [0.6.4] - 2026-11-08

### Fixed

- Harden shell secret masking and tighten predictor hot paths (#20)

## [0.6.3] - 2026-11-01

### Fixed

- **deps:** Support @opentui 0.8 on OpenCode >= 2.2.3 (#17)

## [0.6.2] - 2026-10-27

### Fixed

- **engines:** Require OpenCode >=2.2.0

## [0.6.1] - 2026-10-22

### Fixed

- **prediction:** Correct sentence-start casing, trigram scoring, and next-word filtering

## [0.6.0] - 2026-10-22

### Added

- **completion:** Learn hyphenated words, brand names, filenames and shell commands

## [0.5.2] - 2026-10-22

### Fixed

- **prediction:** Restore personal completion weight, next-word predictions, and slash-command prose

## [0.5.1] - 2026-10-22

### Fixed

- Harden learning persistence and release safety

## [0.5.0] - 2026-10-22

### Added

- **prediction:** Complete learned slash tokens and preserve prior weight

## [0.4.0] - 2026-10-21

### Added

- Add logical-line-end completion and suggestion cycling

## [0.3.4] - 2026-10-21

### Fixed

- Preserve learning exclusions across sync and restart

## [0.3.3] - 2026-10-21

### Fixed

- Keep learning when full, honor clear, and skip subagent sessions
- Hide suggestions that do not fit the cursor row

## [0.3.2] - 2026-10-21

### Added

- Predict words in composers holding attachments or pasted-text chips

## [0.3.1] - 2026-10-20

### Fixed

- **deps:** Require opentui 0.6 for opencode 2.1

## [0.3.0] - 2026-10-15

### Added

- **prediction:** Learn casing, hide fragments, and decay old counts

### Changed

- **learning:** Stop re-sorting sessions once the backfill is seeded

## [0.2.2] - 2026-10-15

### Changed

- **learning:** Read stored snapshots without store proxies

## [0.2.1] - 2026-10-13

### Fixed

- **prediction:** Guard typo corrections and learning races

## [0.2.0] - 2026-10-13

### Added

- **prediction:** Add safe typo correction and context repair

## [0.1.5] - 2026-10-10

### Fixed

- **tui:** Skip history-learning warning for opportunistic syncs

## [0.1.4] - 2026-10-10

### Fixed

- **tui:** Depend on opentui 0.5.x so npm cannot resolve 0.6.0

## [0.1.3] - 2026-10-10

### Fixed

- **tui:** Pin opentui peer dependencies to ^0.5.17 for arborist compatibility

## [0.1.2] - 2026-10-10

### Fixed

- Align peer dependencies with opencode to resolve npm ERESOLVE

## [0.1.1] - 2026-10-10

### Fixed

- **ci:** Handle root commit in commitlint range
- Add `@jsxImportSource @opentui/solid` pragma to the TUI entrypoint so npm cache compilation doesn't fall back to React.
- Constrain `@opentui/core` and `@opentui/solid` peer dependencies to `<0.6.0` with `peerDependenciesMeta` set to optional, preventing conflicting nested OpenTUI versions.
- Support `/quill clear` and `/quill reset` to wipe learned vocabulary and n-gram state.

## [0.1.0] - 2026-10-10

### Added

- Local word autocomplete and next-word prediction plugin for OpenCode V2.
- High-frequency English vocabulary prior derived from SUBTLEX word frequencies.
- Online absolute-discounting n-gram model learning from submitted session prompts.
- Inline ghost-text rendering at visual cursor with matching Ghost dim level (`0.55`).
- Safe acceptance (<kbd>Tab</kbd>, <kbd>→</kbd>) and dismissal (<kbd>Esc</kbd>) without draft submission.
- Prose-aware filtering suppressing suggestions in code, paths, URLs, and shell commands.
- `/quill` command and command palette action to toggle autocomplete.
- Local installer script, full test suite, CI workflows, and release tooling.
